clue.text: A-list chap spending hours upsetting big characters

indicators.note: spending means using up or giving away, so the hours letter is lost from the word for a man

parts.note: a chap is a man or fellow, written in full here before trimming

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over or disturbing, so the letters of A-list are jumbled

explanation.surface: A celebrity type wastes hours being disruptive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending' removes H from CHAP to leave CAP; 'upsetting' rearranges A-LIST into ITALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-case letters are large characters, the kind used at the start of sentences and names.

clue.text: Quartet in concert in days gone by

indicators.note: a quartet is a group of four, here four consecutive letters found inside the word concert

explanation.surface: A string quartet performed in concert long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at some past time, is a common synonym, as in fairy tales beginning that way.

clue.text: Perhaps maiden first wants house to be clean

indicators.note: first tells us the house abbreviation is placed at the front, before the cricket term

parts.note: a maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored, so it is an example of an over

explanation.surface: A young woman wants her house cleaned before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls; a maiden is one where no runs are scored. 'maiden' looks like a young woman but is the cricket term.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark vacuum cleaner name used as a verb means to clean with a vacuum.

clue.text: Work for top people, getting pounds and from 'ere onwards wealth

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
U stands for upper class, the top people
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra
'ence is hence dropping its H in Cockney style, as 'ere is here; hence means from here onwards

explanation.surface: Serving the elite brings money and, from now on, riches.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'ere signals that the synonym hence also loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish richness and affluence is a synonym for great wealth.

clue.text: Native in tin hat surprisingly embracing sailor

indicators.note: embracing means hugging or enclosing, so the anagram goes around the sailor
surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters of in tin hat are rearranged

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a common abbreviation for sailor

explanation.surface: A local in a tin helmet unexpectedly hugs a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges IN TIN HAT into INHITANT, which 'embracing' wraps around AB.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident or person who lives in a place, like a native of it.

clue.text: Scoundrel ordered to get good repeatedly

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered or commanded

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the good abbreviation appears twice in a row

explanation.surface: A villain was told to keep being good.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a rotten, untrustworthy person, a villain or rogue.

clue.text: Easy target making one flap

definitions.meaning: from the idiom about someone who couldn't hit one, something too large to miss
a hinged flap on a stage or studio light that shapes the beam, also the big hinged door of a farm building

explanation.surface: An easy mark causes someone to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially the biggest, easiest thing to hit, and also a hinged flap fitted to a lamp.

clue.text: Mark in playing field north of old road

indicators.note: in a down clue north of means placed above, so the field comes first

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a playing field

explanation.surface: A marking on a sports field lies just north of an ancient road.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a British recreation ground, a public park for games.
explanation.definitionFit: A best-ever performance or achievement is a mark that others try to beat.

clue.text: Joke precedes brief medical procedure in subcontinental area

indicators.note: precedes means comes before, so the joke comes first

parts.note: a pun is a joke made on words
a jab is an injection, a quick medical procedure

explanation.surface: A quip before a quick injection somewhere in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A region in the north of the Indian subcontinent, split between India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Hurry around very busy place

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the hurry word goes around the very abbreviation

parts.note: hie is an old word for hurry

explanation.surface: Rush around a very crowded location.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee colony's home, used figuratively for any bustling centre of activity.

clue.text: Unwell after brief holiday, an old rocker hesitated

indicators.note: after tells us the unwell word comes after the holiday

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday
ill means unwell
a Ted or Teddy boy was a 1950s rock and roll fan

explanation.surface: After a short break, an ageing rock fan felt ill and dithered.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth subculture tied to rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver between choices is a synonym for dithering or hesitating.

clue.text: Distant sea abroad for one normally on the land

parts.note: far means distant
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A faraway foreign sea suits someone usually ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: An agricultural worker spends their life working the soil rather than at sea.

clue.text: What when drunk is crimson, aha!

definitions.text: What when drunk is crimson, aha!

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and unsteady, so the letters of crimson aha are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drinker exclaims at something that turns red when consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry liqueur, and the bright red preserved cherries soaked in it, fit the description.

clue.text: Positions organised by Cambridge college?

parts.note: ran means managed or organised
King's is a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: Places in a league table arranged by a university college.
explanation.definitionFit: Places held in an ordered list or league table are positions.

clue.text: Vehicle by front of shop gets bashed

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of the word shop

parts.note: a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A lorry by a shop front gets damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit or knocked hard, the past tense of strike, matches bashed.

clue.text: Small openings? Girl being stuck inside yells

indicators.note: being stuck inside means placed within, so the girl goes into the yells word

parts.note: cries means yells
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl trapped indoors shouts for help.
explanation.definitionFit: Small gaps or chinks, as in nooks and these, are narrow openings.

clue.text: Within a week, say, business area goes to rack and ruin

indicators.note: within means inside, so the business area sits inside the days

parts.note: a week is an example of a span of days
EC is the postcode for the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Inside seven days the commercial district falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the London postcode covering the City, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot or decline into a ruined state matches going to rack and ruin.

clue.text: The female somehow hated being wrapped up

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters of hated are rearranged

explanation.surface: The woman somehow loathed being bundled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Encased in a cover, as a sword in its scabbard, is to be wrapped up.

clue.text: Very happy to be as one of the family but not the head of it

indicators.note: not the head of it means the first letter of the family word is dropped

parts.note: related means belonging to the same family

explanation.surface: Delighted to belong to the family, though not to lead it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the head of it' removes the R from RELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Overjoyed or thrilled, a synonym for very happy.

clue.text: US general with a plan taking everyone to swampy area

parts.note: a marsh is a swampy area
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A general leads all his troops into a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: George C. Marshall, the American general, gave his name to the post-war European recovery plan.

clue.text: One from hot dusty place goes to the foreign land where things can grow

parts.note: an Arab is someone from Arabia, a hot dusty desert region
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A desert dweller moves to a fertile foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland suitable for ploughing and growing crops is known by this term.

clue.text: Perhaps a trimmer sort of vessel

definitions.meaning: one who trims or snips, for example a hairdresser or tailor
a small fast boat, such as a coastguard ship

explanation.surface: A neater kind of boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both someone who snips things and a small, fast sailing ship share this name.

clue.text: Box of paintings maybe in study

indicators.note: in means inside, so the art goes inside the study word

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: A crate of pictures sits in someone's den.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard container, such as one holding milk or eggs, is a kind of box.

clue.text: Leader of men taking a country to right is seen as a plotter

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word men

parts.note: China is a country

explanation.surface: A ruler who leads a nation to the political right is viewed as a schemer.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer who devises cunning plans or intrigues is a plotter.

clue.text: It's the end of the game, chum

definitions.text: It's the end of the game
definitions.meaning: checkmate ends a chess game, often shortened

explanation.surface: Game over, my friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess's final checkmating move and a friendly word for a pal share this spelling.

clue.text: Frenzy brought by smell of dampness

definitions.meaning: a state of frenzied aggression in male elephants or camels during the rutting season
a stale mouldy odour from damp

explanation.surface: Madness induced by a mouldy odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rutting elephant's frenzied state, and a stale mouldy smell, share this word.

clue.text: A batsman's stroke, look

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a deflecting shot that angles the ball off the bat

explanation.surface: A cricketer plays a shot and peeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A deflecting cricket shot and a brief look both go by this name.

clue.text: Where milk is left and a chunk of bread

definitions.meaning: the step outside the front door where milk deliveries are left
a very thick slice of bread

explanation.surface: The milkman leaves bottles and a hunk of loaf at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain milk is traditionally delivered to the front step of homes.
explanation.definitionFit: The step at a front door, and informally a thick slice of bread, share this name.
